title: Transport Properties of Ibuprofen Encapsulated in Cyclodextrin Nanosponge Hydrogels: A Proton HR-MAS NMR Spectroscopy Study
protocol: Dry β-cyclodextrin (β-CD) in an oven at 80°C for 4 hours before use.
Dry 500 ml of dimethylsulfoxide (DMSO) and 100 ml of triethylamine (Et3N) over molecular sieves (4 Å) for 24 hours before using them.
Introduce 25 ml of DMSO into a 50 ml one-neck round-bottom flask under magnetic stirring.
Add β-CD powder in small portions to the homogeneous solution of DMSO until all is added, taking approximately 30 minutes.
After 30 minutes, add 6 ml of Et3N to the solution using a 10 ml graduated pipette and keep under stirring for 15 minutes at room temperature (RT).
Plunge the flask into a water bath at RT.
Add 5.124 g of EDTA-dianhydride or 10.248 g of EDTA-dianhydride to the solution under intense stirring, depending on whether CDNSEDTA 1:4 or 1:8 is prepared.
After 3 hours, remove the solid material (CDNSEDTA 1:4 or 1:8) from the flask using a spatula and crush it grossly with a mortar and pestle.
Wash the solid material onto filter paper with acetone at RT (100 ml × 5 times).
Wash the solid material with HCl 0.1 M (200 ml × 5 times) at RT.
Wash the solid material with deionized water (200 ml × 3 times) at RT.
Dry all the solid material in air at RT for 48 hours.
Crush the dried solid material finely into a mortar and pestle.
Keep the finely crushed solid under vacuum (<15 mbar) for 2 hours at 45°C.
Prepare a solution of 0.27 M ibuprofen sodium salt in deuterated water (99.8%).
Add 20 mg of CDNSEDTA 1:4 and 2 mg of anhydrous Sodium carbonate to 150 μl of the ibuprofen sodium salt solution.
Mix the content of the vial with a small spatula to homogenize it.
Wait 2 hours before using the gel formed with this procedure.
Repeat the preparation for CDNSEDTA 1:8 polymer.
Insert the gel in a 5 mm NMR rotor suitable for HR-MAS NMR experiments using a small spatula.
Set the rotor spinning speed of 4 KHz at the MAS pneumatic control unit.
Set the sample temperature to 305 K in the variable temperature unit.
Acquire the 1H HR-MAS NMR spectra of ibuprofen in CDNSEDTA (1:4) and CDNSEDTA (1:8) polymer systems using a conventional one pulse sequence on the proton resonance.
Create a new data set.
Click on the "AcquPars" tab.
Select the PULPROG: zg.
Select the number of scans (NS = 4).
Set the time delay between scans (D1 = 5 sec).
Set the spectral width (SW = 8 ppm).
Set the time domain (TD = 16K).
Set the receiver gain (RG = 32).
Type "zg" on the console.
Observe a free induction decay (FID) on the screen.
To process the data, click on the "ProcPars" tab.
Set the spectral size (SI = 32K).
Select an exponential multiplication window function (WDW = EM).
Apply line broadening (LB = 1).
Type "ft" to perform the Fourier transformation.
Phase the spectrum using the phase tab on the screen.
Obtain a high resolution well resolved spectrum.
Create a new data set - experiment number 1.
Click on the "AcquPars" tab.
Select PULPROG: ledbpgp2s1d pulse sequence for diffusion optimization.
Set the number of scans (NS) to 16.
Set the time delay between scans (D1) to 10 seconds.
Set the spectral width (SW) to 8 ppm.
Set the time domain (TD) to 16K.
Set the receiver gain (RG) to 32.
Set Δ (D20 in the sequence) to a constant value of 50 msec.
Set δ (p30) to an initial trial value of 3 msec.
Read the spectral frequency (SFO1) from the 1H experiment and use it for the current setup.
Set the GPZ6 gradient strength to 2%.
Repeat steps with different values of δ to optimize parameters.
Use the resulting spectrum as a reference for further optimization.
Create experiment number 2.
Observe all experimental parameters.
Increase GPZ6 gradient strength to 95%.
Repeat step 2.2.2.3.
Compare the spectrum with the reference spectrum using the dual display icon.
Observe the change in signal intensity.
If signal intensity is lost, reduce δ and restart section 2.3.1 from point 2.3.1.3.
Optimize parameters for Δ values of 50, 80, 110, 140, and 170 msec.
For IP in CDNSEDTA 1:8, optimize δ to 3, 2.7, 2.4, 2.1, 1.8 msec respectively for each Δ value.
For IP in CDNSEDTA 1:4, optimize δ to 2.7, 2.4, 2, 1.7, 1.4 msec respectively for each Δ value.
Create experiment number 3.
Load all 1D experimental parameters.
Type "eda".
Select PULPROG: ledbpgp2s pulse sequence.
Change parmode to 2D.
Set FnMODE=QF.
Set time domain TD in F2 dimension equal to 32, the number of gradient steps.
Type "DOSY" and generate the gradient ramp.
Store the gradient ramp values (2 - 95).
Start acquisition.
Execute the Fourier transformation in the F2 dimension.
Perform baseline correction in the F2 dimension.
Recall experimental parameters (Δ, δ, and gradient list) for the next processing step.
Click "T1/T2 relaxation module" in the analysis tab.
Define peaks to be fitted using the first spectrum of the 2D experiment.
Define peak ranges.
Execute fitting.
Obtain signal intensities at each applied gradient step.
Export signal intensities in a spreadsheet.
Perform linear fit of the data to get the value of z² for each observed diffusion time td.
Perform the log-log plot of z2 versus td for each experimental td value.
Calculate the exponent α as the slope of the linear regression line.
